Smt. Urmila And Others vs State Of U.P. And Others on 18 July,
2023
Author: Saumitra Dayal Singh

Bench: Saumitra Dayal Singh
High Court Of Judicature At Allahabad
Neutral Citation No. - 2023:Ahc:142420-Db
Court No. - 39
Case :- Writ - C No. - 29373 of 2011
Petitioner :- Smt. Urmila And Others
Respondent :- State of U.P. and Others
Counsel for Petitioner :- N.D. Shukla
Counsel for Respondent :- C.S.C.
Hon'ble Saumitra Dayal Singh,J.
Hon'ble Vinod Diwakar,J.

entities.text: High Court Of Judicature At Allahabad
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: 1. Heard Sri N.D. Shukla, learned counsel for the petitioners and Sri Piyush Srivastava, learned Standing Counsel for the State.

2. The present petition has been filed seeking a direction to the respondents to pay adequate and full compensation to the petitioners with respect to Plot No.258 area .02585 hectare, village Majhgawa,
Tehsil Gyanpur, Bhadohi, which is described to have been forcibly taken over by the respondent State-authority to construct a police station.

Further prayer made in the writ petition is regarding Smt. Urmila And Others vs State Of U.P. And Others on 18 July, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/173855197/
1 payment of interest claimed at the rate of 15% from the date of possession i.e. 25.2.1997 till date together with 9% additional interest.

entities.text: Smt. Urmila And Others vs State Of U.P. And Others
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 3. Earlier, the petitioners had approached this Court by means of writ petition being Writ Petition No.25094 of 2007.

The said writ petition was disposed of by this Court vide order dated 16.2.2009,
which reads as under:
"Heard learned counsel for the petitioners and learned standing counsel representing the respondent nos.1 to 5 and perused the record.
The grievance of the petitioners is that the police station is being constructed over their land without making acquisition of the same.
Since the establishment of the police station is in the larger public interest & for public purpose therefore, we are not inclined to interfere with the construction.

It is however, provided that Collector will look into the matter and pass appropriate orders in accordance with law on the representations of the petitioners which shall be filed together with certified copy of this order and in case the Collector comes to the conclusion that the police station is being constructed over the land of the petitioner

,
the petitioners shall be paid compensation within three months from the date of passing of the order by the Collector provided if the compensation is not already paid to the petitioners."
4.
In compliance thereto, the Collector, Bhadohi passed order dated 18.7.2009 providing for total compensation of Rs.5,11,290/-.
That amount is disclosed to have been paid to the petitioners on 31.3.2010.

5. Though the petitioners have filed the present writ petition seeking the reliefs noted above, today upon the matter being taken up for hearing, up to the completion of submissions, Sri N.D. Shukla,
learned counsel for the petitioners chose to press only one relief, namely, demand of interest and solatium However, after the submissions advanced by the learned Standing Counsel, learned counsel for the petitioners even without seeking leave of the Court, added the submission with respect to inadequacy of the compensation.
Though deprecated and not expected from such a senior counsel appearing in Court regularly, we have allowed that submission to be raised purely in the interest of justice.
However, the Court must record its displeasure at the manner the senior counsel has chosen to appear and taken the Court proceedings casually.
The conduct offered by the senior counsel sets a bad example for the younger members of the Bar to follow.
It is for the members of the Bar to reflect their fair conduct while appearing in the Court proceedings.

6. Leaving the issue apart, the bare facts of the case are that the petitioners were the recorded tenure holders of Plot No.258 admeasuring 1 bigha, 2 biswa and 11 dhur, village Majhgawa, Tehsil Gyanpur, Bhadohi.

Earlier vide order dated 25.2.1997 passed by the Sub Divisional Magistrate,
Gyanpur, Bhadohi in Case No.5 of 1996, under Section 161 Uttar Pradesh Zamindari Abolition and Land Reforms Act, 1950 (hereinafter referred to as "the Act"), certain exchange of land was Smt. Urmila And Others vs State Of U.P. And Others on 18 July, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/173855197/
2 recorded.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Insofar as present case is concerned, the petitioners' rights in Plot No.258 were exchanged and they were recorded as tenure holder of Plot No.241 admeasuring 1 bigha only.
Prior to the exchange being recorded, the Police Station Koirana was recorded as the owner over 2 bighas of Plot No.241.

The plots were exchanged and the names of the petitioners were recorded on Plot No.241 over area about 1 bigha only.
7.

At the same time, a perusal of the contents of paragraph 4 of the counter affidavit and its reply contained in paragraph 13 of the rejoinder affidavit indicate that the order dated 25.2.1997 was never challenged or assailed by the petitioners.
8. It is in above fact background, a dispute arose at the instance of the petitioners with respect to their alleged forcible eviction over plot No.258 admeasuring 1 bigha 2 biswa and 11 dhur.

The petitioners' claim, they had been forcibly evicted from the plot in question without there being any proceedings drawn under the Land Acquisition Act, 1894 and without any award being made or compensation paid to them.
In that circumstance, earlier writ petition filed by the petitioners was disposed of by this Court with a direction to the respondent State-authority to pay adequate compensation.
9. That amount of compensation has been quantified by the impugned order dated 18.7.2009, at Rs.5,11,290/-.
In doing that, the Collector has considered the claim setup by the petitioners in their representation dated 18.6.2009.
Perusal of the said representation reveals, the petitioners only demanded compensation.
No specific prayer for interest or solatium was made.
Yet reliance has been placed on a decision of the Supreme Court in Sukh Dutt Ratra and another v. State of Himachal Pradesh and others, (2022) 7 SCC 508.

entities.text: Sukh Dutt Ratra and another v. State of Himachal Pradesh and others, (2022) 7 SCC 508
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Further reliance has been placed on the decision of coordinate Bench of this Court in Shiva Nand Gupta and another v. State of U.P. and others, 2014 (6) ADJ 396.

entities.text: Shiva Nand Gupta and another v. State of U.P. and others, 2014 (6) ADJ 396
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: It has further been prayed that cost may also be awarded against the respondent State-authority for gross illegal act performed by them.
As to the award of compensation, it has vehemently been urged that the same is inadequate.
Relying on the Government Order dated 19.3.2015, it has been submitted, the award ought to have been determined at four times the Circle Rate, since the land is situate in rural area.

10. On the other hand, learned Standing Counsel would submit, in the first place, the petitioners had no right to be compensated as the land over which the Police Station has been constructed, had been recorded in the name of the police station upon the order dated 25.2.1997 being passed by the Collector in Case No.5 of 1996 instituted under Section 161 of the Act.
Second, in any case, the amount of compensation has been determined at the Circle Rate prevailing in the year 2008.
Over and above that, 20% additional amount has been paid towards solatium.
If the proceedings were to be treated in accordance with Land Acquisition Act, 1894, the valuation of land would have been far less of the year 1995.
Therefore, the computation of compensation awarded may not be described as inadequate.
Third, it has been submitted, the Government Order dated 19.3.2015 has no application to the present case.
It is nothing more than a policy decision taken in March, 2015, to be applied prospectively.
Since, the transaction took place in 1998 and computation of the compensation was made in the year 2008, the said Government Order is of no relevance.

Even otherwise, the said Government Order may not have any applicability to force computation of any amount of Smt. Urmila And Others vs State Of U.P. And Others on 18 July, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/173855197/
3 compensation since the policy decision was for determination of amount of compensation to be paid on agreed basis.

entities.text: Smt. Urmila And Others vs State Of U.P. And Others
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
As to the demand of payment of interest, it has been submitted, once the petitioners have availed the benefit of higher compensation computed at rates that prevailed more than 13 years after land had been acquired, if at all, that claim is wholly misconceived.
11.

Having heard learned counsel for the parties and having perused the record, it may not be denied that the citizen may remain entitled to receive compensation to be computed in accordance with law in lieu of any land forcibly taken over.
That is the law laid down by the Supreme Court in Sukh Dutt Ratra's case (supra).
In para 23 of the said judgment, it was observed as under "23.

This court, in Vidya Devi (supra) facing an almost identical set of facts and circumstances - rejected the contention of 'oral' consent to be baseless and outlined the responsibility of the State:
"12.9.
In a democratic polity governed by the rule of law, the State could not have deprived a citizen of their property without the sanction of law.

Reliance is placed on the judgment of this Court in Tukaram Kana Joshi v. MIDC [Tukaram Kana Joshi v. MIDC, (2013) 1 SCC 353 : (2013) 1 SCC (Civ)
491] wherein it was held that the State must comply with the procedure for acquisition, requisition,
or any other permissible statutory mode.

entities.text:
Tukaram Kana Joshi v. MIDC [Tukaram Kana Joshi v. MIDC, (2013) 1 SCC 353 : (2013) 1 SCC (Civ)
491
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The State being a welfare State governed by the rule of law cannot arrogate to itself a status beyond what is provided by the Constitution.

This Court in State of Haryana v. Mukesh Kumar [State of Haryana v. Mukesh Kumar, (2011)
10 SCC 404 : (2012) 3 SCC (Civ) 769] held that the right to property is now considered to be not only a constitutional or statutory right, but also a human right.

entities.text:
State of Haryana v. Mukesh Kumar [State of Haryana v. Mukesh Kumar, (2011)
10 SCC 404 : (2012) 3 SCC (Civ) 769]
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Human rights have been considered in the realm of individual rights such as right to shelter, livelihood, health, employment, etc.

Human rights have gained a multi-faceted dimension."
12.

Thereafter by way of conclusion, it was recorded as below:
"25.

Concluding that the forcible dispossession of a person of their private property without following due process of law, was violative of both their human right, and constitutional right under Article 300-A, this court allowed the appeal.
We find that the approach taken by this court in Vidya Devi (supra) is squarely applicable to the nearly identical facts before us in the present case.

26. In view of the above discussion, in view of this court's extraordinary jurisdiction under Article 136 and 142 of the Constitution, the State is hereby directed to treat the subject lands as a deemed acquisition and appropriately disburse compensation to the appellants in the same terms as the order of the reference court dated 04.10.2005 in Land Ref. Petition No. 10-LAC/4 of 2004 (and consolidated matters).

The Respondent-State is directed, consequently to ensure that the appropriate Land Acquisition Collector computes the compensation, and disburses it to the appellants,
within four months from today.

The appellants would also be entitled to consequential benefits of solatium, and interest on all sums payable under law w.e.f Smt. Urmila And Others vs State Of U.P. And Others on 18 July, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/173855197/
4 16.10.2001 (i.e. date of issuance of notification under Section 4 of the Act), till the date of the impugned judgment, i.e. 12.09.2013."

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 13. The Supreme Court in Tukaram Kana Joshi and others v. Maharashtra Industrial Development Corporation and others, (2013) 1 SCC 353 and in Bhimandas Ambwani (dead) through LRs v. Delhi Power Company Limited, (2013) 14 SCC 195 had also taken a view similar to the reasoning given by the Supreme Court in Sukh Dutt Ratra's case (supra).

entities.text: Tukaram Kana Joshi and others v. Maharashtra Industrial Development Corporation and others, (2013) 1 SCC 353
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Therefore, by way of principle, it may never be denied that the petitioners' land had been taken over by the respondents, forcibly, without following due process.
Therefore, the State-authority would remain liable to compensate the petitioners for such an act.
There can arise no issue as to the application of that principle.

However, as to the computation of the compensation, it also cannot be denied that the Circle Rate to be applied or exemplar to be considered for the purposes of computation of compensation, if the present proceeding has arisen in accordance with the provisions of Land Acquisition Act would be of the date prior to issuance of the notification.
14. According to the petitioners, they lost the possession over the land in the year 1997.
The Circle Rate of the land that would have increased thereafter, would be immaterial to determine compensation in such proceedings, if they had arisen.
15. In the present case, bare perusal of the order dated 18.7.2009 reveals that the Collector took note of Circle Rate applicable to the land in the year 2008.
Therefore, a higher Circle Rate had been applied to the petitioners' case while determining the compensation awarded.
Moreover, upon that rate being applied and certain objections arising, 20% increment was made towards solatium.
It is that rate of computation that led to determination of the award of compensation of Rs.5,11,269/-.
Undisputedly, the same was paid out to the petitioners.

16. Thus, we may record that a higher amount of compensation than may have been computed in accordance with Land Acquisition Act, has been paid out to the petitioners by way of compensation and solatium.
17. It is also undisputed, the land of the petitioners had been exchanged and in that regard no averments have even been disclosed in the writ petition.
At the same time, the existence of the order dated 25.2.1997 providing for such exchange is not disputed.
It is also not disputed that the petitioners did not have surviving rights in plot no.258.

Further, it is also not disputed that earlier,
in exchange thereof the petitioners received rights in plot no. 241 admeasuring 1 bigha.
Those rights appear to have remained undisturbed, despite the compensation being awarded to the petitioners.

18. Thus, we do not find the present case to be a fit case where we may exercise extraordinary powers of the Court under Article 226 of the Constitution of India to award interest over an amount that we prima facie find was in excess of the legal entitlement of the petitioners.
The interference claimed, is thus declined.
19. The writ petition is dismissed.
No order as to costs.
